description: MassMotion is a commercial pedestrian simulation and crowd modelling program from Oasys, used by engineers, designers, planners, architects and operators to design spaces around the people who use them. Users import 2D or 3D geometry from BIM and CAD files such as FBX, IFC and DWG, add real-world data on population, demographics and schedules, and run scenarios of pedestrian movement and operations. Results come as tables, heatmaps and graphs showing congestion hot spots, wait times, trip times and other spatial performance measures, and agents can be shown as 3D avatars for flythrough videos. A software development kit gives direct access to the simulation engine, its algorithms and agents so that it can be built into other workflows. Coverage: any building, station or public space the user models. Access: licences through Oasys, which invites contact on the product page. Licence: commercial; the price is not published on the page read. Caveats: closed source; the provider states validated accuracy, but the validation evidence was not read on the day. Simulation uses are crowd flow and evacuation in stations, venues and large buildings, and testing operational scenarios such as closures. Related records: the Pathfinder record and the physics-based pedestrian modelling record.
